title: Counter-light Memory Encryption
problem: Counterless memory encryption stalls on cache misses because cipher calculations require data from memory as input, causing ~9% slowdown on irregular workloads. Counter mode avoids this but incurs memory access overhead.
motivation: Memory encryption is essential for CPU security (SGX, SEV), but current approaches force a tradeoff between efficient memory access and fast cryptographic calculations.
method: Counter-light Encryption hybridizes counter mode and counterless encryption by storing counters on-chip to enable pre-computation of cipher calculations before data arrives from memory, while maintaining efficient memory access patterns. This selectively applies counter mode's cipher-calculation parallelism to reduce cache miss stalls.
key_novelty: Combining counter mode and counterless encryption to achieve cipher calculation parallelism of counter mode with the memory access efficiency of counterless mode.
contributions: Hybrid encryption scheme combining counter and counterless approaches
Analysis of counterless encryption's cache miss bottleneck (9% overhead)
